issues.description: The problem statement's UML and the reference solution define Stock.take(String) to return an int (using -1 to indicate failure), but the template implementation declares Stock.take(String) to return a boolean. This mismatch will confuse students: the UML/spec expects an int return value and the solution relies on int semantics (checking for -1), while the template forces a boolean API and different behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template Stock.take(String) signature to return int (matching the UML and solution). Implement it to return -1 when the ingredient is not found or quantity is insufficient, and otherwise decrement the quantity and return the remaining quantity. Also update any code that calls take(...) to check for -1 rather than using boolean logic (this will align the template with the specification and the provided solution).

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies Stock.take(String): int but the template Stock.take method returns boolean. The solution implements Stock.take(String): int (returning -1 on failure). This mismatch in the method's return type and failure convention across artifacts creates a mapping and implementation confusion for students: they will expect an int-based API (as documented) while the provided template uses a boolean API, causing semantic and possible compile-time inconsistencies when implementing SealSaloon logic that relies on integer return values.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Stock.take method with the problem statement and solution by changing its signature to return int. Use the same convention as the solution: return -1 when the ingredient is missing or insufficient, otherwise decrement quantity and return the new quantity. Update any code comments or examples in the template to reflect the int-based contract.
